atAGlance: Vegetarian phở with rice noodles, herbs, and a lighter broth built from vegetables, mushrooms, and warm spices instead of beef bones.
whatItIs: Phở chay keeps the recognizable phở shape: flat noodles, fragrant broth, herbs, lime, and chili, but it swaps meat for tofu, mushrooms, vegetables, or plant-based toppings.
howToEnjoy: Taste the broth first; good phở chay gets sweetness from vegetables and depth from mushrooms. Add herbs and lime gradually so the gentle broth stays balanced.
howLocalsOrder: Order phở with the vegetarian request clearly so the shop understands you want the vegetarian version, not just extra vegetables. If you avoid fish sauce, ask whether fish sauce is used before adding any dip or broth seasoning.
worthKnowing: Chay food is especially visible around Buddhist observance days, and dishes like phở chay let travelers experience familiar Vietnamese forms through temple and vegetarian cooking traditions.
goodToKnow: Ask whether the broth is vegetable-based and whether fish sauce is used in seasoning if you need it fully vegetarian.
travelerCaution: Confirm the broth and seasoning are vegetarian if strict.
